normalization_policy: normalized claim plus artifact and evidence target; no voting

findings.claim: P16 permits an alternate task acceptance owner named by any non-revoked HUMAN authority decision, without requiring that decision to originate from the designated mission decision owner or a hash-pinned delegation chain from that owner, unlike P13 and the Section 16 WBS-build entry criteria.
findings.evidence_excerpt: an alternate with `actor.kind = human` explicitly named by a separate non-revoked HUMAN authority decision ID/raw hash and exact task/scope
findings.impact: A HUMAN record outside the mission decision owner chain can satisfy the P16 charge-time invariant and later grant acceptance, so acceptance can be produced without the designated owner authority even though Section 16 requires an owner-rooted chain that P16 does not enforce at admission.
findings.recommended_action: Bind every alternate acceptor in P16 and Section 5.4 to the designated mission decision owner through a complete hash-pinned non-revoked HUMAN delegation chain with exact task/scope, matching P13, and re-verify that chain at P14 and at the acceptance boundary.

findings.claim: P15 enumerates approved argv hashes for validator, prepare, bundle-seal, invalidation, admin-ledger-append and charge-preimage-seal, but omits the AIP pointer/ASC `run_aip.py step|resume` transition that Section 5.1(a) declares as one of the four pre-charge writes separately approved under P15.
findings.impact: The FROZEN-to-PREPARING AIP pointer/ASC write can occur without the pinned HUMAN-approved argv/tool hash that P15 requires for the other three pre-charge writes, so that generated-AIP/ASC control write is not bound to the P15 approved-capability set.
findings.recommended_action: Add the exact AIP pointer/ASC `run_aip.py step|resume` argv/tool hash and its bounded pointer/ASC/Workspace effect to the P15 and `bootstrap_authority` approved-capability enumeration, or drop the assertion that write (a) is separately approved under P15.

findings.claim: Section 12.5 and the admission state machine direct a charged attempt whose reviewer route is lost into REVIEW_PENDING, but neither the state machine nor the Section 14 recovery matrix declares an owner, escalation, exit or closure disposition for REVIEW_PENDING.
findings.evidence_excerpt: If no eligible route remains, enter `REVIEW_PENDING`; never substitute an unbound placeholder packet.
findings.impact: Reviewer loss after charge leaves a charged attempt without a declared recovery or terminal disposition, so the mission cannot deterministically resolve the attempt, and the must-check reviewer-loss negative path is incomplete.
findings.recommended_action: Declare the REVIEW_PENDING owner, bounded re-probe/retry rule, route-restoration exit, HUMAN escalation and terminal disposition in the state machine, Section 12 and Section 14.

findings.claim: P3 defines lineage for charge successors and POST_CHARGE_REPAIR but omits the ordinary post-charge execution.json status, outcome, review, and acceptance writes that the design itself authorizes.
findings.evidence_excerpt: allowing only the Section 5.2 hash-complete `POST_CHARGE_REPAIR` exceptional link that preserves the same attempt/charge
findings.impact: After a normal charged attempt changes outcome or acceptance state, the next admission must either reject the ledger as non-append divergence or silently admit an unproved lineage exception, defeating multi-attempt closure.
findings.recommended_action: Define source, candidate, persisted hashes and receipts for every authorized execution.json transition and make P3 accept only that complete chain, or isolate an append-only event history with a deterministically rebuilt current projection.

findings.claim: The migration protocol hard-codes dsh-wbs-execution/1 as its target even though P15 permits a different versioned execution-contract extension when v1 lacks the required charge, bundle, seal, and lineage representation.
findings.evidence_excerpt: 2. Pin the authoritative target `dsh-wbs-execution/1` contract/tool version.
findings.impact: If existing v1 pointers cannot be proven, option (b) has no declared one-time migration target; the flow either migrates twice, deadlocks bootstrap against migration, or invents fields in v1.
findings.recommended_action: Make migration step 2 consume the HUMAN-approved P15 representation decision and pin either proven v1 pointers plus fixture or the exact extension contract, validator, and migration bytes before any transformation.

findings.claim: The closed pre-charge write set permits only run_aip step or resume, while the artifact-ownership policy also permits start, leaving a fresh Working AIP without one unambiguous admission state and effect rule.
findings.impact: A successor execution needing first-time AIP initialization must either perform an undeclared pre-charge control write or remain NOT_READY; treating the broader Section 10 command set as authority breaks the four-effect closure.
findings.recommended_action: Either add start to the P15-authorized FROZEN-to-PREPARING effect with the same path, hash, sequence, epoch, and no-charge receipt limits, or require proof that the AIP was already started before FROZEN and remove start from the admission command set.
